{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Test

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        os: [macos-latest, windows-latest, ubuntu-latest]

    steps:
      - name: Check out Git repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v1

      - name: Checkout submodules
        run: git submodule update --init --recursive

      - name: Install Linux dependencies
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: sudo apt-get update -y && sudo apt-get install -y libasound2-dev

      - name: Install Node.js and NPM
        uses: actions/setup-node@v2
        with:
          node-version: 16
          cache: npm

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v4 # https://github.com/nodejs/node-gyp/issues/2869
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'

      - name: npm install
        run: |
          npm install

      - name: npm test
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

        # npm run lint
        # npm test
        run: |
          npm run package
          npm exec tsc",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs a three-OS matrix with no fail-fast policy, so all jobs continue even after one fails. The P-LIT-FAIL-FAST pattern supports cancelling remaining matrix jobs after a failure to save CI resources while preserving the merge decision (a failed job still blocks the PR). Adding fail-fast: true is a minimal change that keeps every build and test step intact, does not weaken permissions, and adds no privileged actions, secrets, or network access.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-FAIL-FAST"]
}
